birth.place: San Mango d'Aquino, Catanzaro, Calabria, Italy

summary: Emigrant from San Mango d'Aquino in Calabria to Scranton's Providence section and father of Helen (Ferlaino) Cognetti; John's maternal 2nd-great-grandfather.
bio:
Leopoldo Ferlaino was baptized at the parish of San Tommaso d'Aquino in San Mango d'Aquino, Calabria, on 25 July 1871, the son of Fortunato Ferlaino and Rosa Moraca; his godparents were Nicola Perri and his wife Rosa Berardelli. His parents had lost an earlier son of the same name, baptized in February 1870, who died at five months old that July. His other brothers and sisters were Gennaro (1855), Raffaela (1858), Marianna (1865) and Giuseppe Antonio (1868). The Ferlainos were long established in San Mango: the parish's rolls of souls from 1674 to 1804 hold 229 entries for the name, among them Francesco Ferlaino and Fragostina Colosimo with their children Carmine, Giuseppe Antonio and others between 1771 and 1788, and the family was still numerous in the town in the 1990s.

Leopoldo married Giuseppina Fiorillo (1871–1943), perhaps civilly only or in another parish, since the marriage does not appear among San Mango's church marriages. Their daughter Maria Filomena, later known as Helen, was born at San Mango on 8 October 1894, the only child of theirs baptized there. By about 1901 he had settled in Scranton, Pennsylvania, where his children Frank (about 1902–03) and Raffaela (about 1904–05) were born; the family home was on Diamond Avenue in the Providence section, where his widow still headed the household in 1920. In America the name was sometimes written Farino.

He died on 2 November 1915 at Dickson City, a borough adjoining North Scranton. His daughter Helen apparently named her fifth son, Leopold Salvatore, after him.

researchNotes:
Tree: Leopoldo Ferlaino (1871-1915) + Giuseppina Fiorillo (1871-1943), parents of Helen. Round 1 found no public record naming him or his wife and could not establish where he died in 1915 (Scranton or San Mango); the Diamond Avenue Ferlaino household was a speculative candidate for their home. Round 2: his widow headed 1306 Diamond Ave in 1920; his PA-born children Frank (c.1902-03) and Raffaela (c.1904-05) show he was in Scranton by about 1901. Helen's fifth son Leopold Salvatore was apparently named for him. San Mango cemetery index has no Leopoldo or Giuseppina, consistent with both dying in Scranton. No published FS profile under Ferlaino, Farino, Farina or Fiorillo with a Scranton tie. Antenati's San Mango coverage ends in 1860, so his 1871 birth and the Ferlaino x Fiorillo marriage (c.1890-95) cannot be reached there. Ferlaino is genuinely a San Mango family: the stati delle anime 1674-1804 have 229 Ferlaino entries (e.g. Francesco Ferlaino and Fragostina Colosimo with children Carmine, Giuseppe Antonio and others, 1771-88); a mid-1990s phone directory shows Ferlaino x24.

Leopoldo was baptized at San Mango d'Aquino on 25 July 1871 as the son of Fortunato Ferlaino and Rosa Moraca. The godparents were Nicola Perri and his wife Rosa Berardelli. I read the entry on the register photograph ([R4-S1], [R4-S2]). His parents had lost an earlier son named Leopoldo: baptized in February 1870, that child died at five months in July 1870 ([R4-S4], [R4-S5]). The parish index lists his other siblings as Gennaro (1855), Raffaela (1858), Marianna (1865) and Giuseppe Antonio (1868) ([R4-S6]). His only child baptized at San Mango was Maria Filomena (later Helen), born 8 October 1894 ([R4-S7]). No church marriage of Leopoldo and Giuseppina Fiorillo appears in the San Mango marriage index for 1885-1920, so they may have married civilly only, or in another parish. The Pennsylvania death-certificate index for 1915 has 'Ferlaino, Leopoldo; 104147; Dickson City; Nov. 2' ([R4-S3]). Dickson City is a borough adjoining North Scranton. This fixes his death as 2 November 1915, in Pennsylvania rather than Italy, and gives the certificate number.
